messages:
maria: FYI — new tenant onboarding (acme-inc) is failing during SCIM provisioning with 403s right after the KMS alias rotation earlier today. SAML login works for users.
kevin: curious — 403 on SCIM only? can you paste the provisioner logs?
maria: here are the tail lines from the scim-provisioner svc (redacted):
```
2026-03-21T18:05:11.123Z ERROR scim-provisioner: POST /scim/v2/Users 403 - audit_id=af2b1c - user=svc-scim@acme - error=KMSDecryptError: FailedUnwrapKey
2026-03-21T18:05:11.125Z WARN  scim-provisioner: KMS context mismatch for alias redwood/acme-rotation-2026
2026-03-21T18:05:11.126Z DEBUG auth: token unwrap failed, err=invalid_encryption_context
```
maria: provisioning process immediately returns 403, no retry. queue builds up.
idp-bot: SAML assertion validation OK for subject=alice@acme.com at 18:04:58 (assertion-id=...), authn method=urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport
jen: audit logs show the scim service-account got DENY from KMS at the same time: 
"principals": ["svc-scim@acme"], "action": "Decrypt", "result": "AccessDenied", "reason": "encryption-context mismatch"
kevin: encryption-context mismatch — that usually means the key alias changed semantics or the envelope metadata we pass during encrypt/unlock changed. Did we change any context keys during rotation?
liz: I pushed the rotation earlier this morning. I only swapped alias pointer to the new key in KMS; didn't touch the provisioner config. I did update the kms-alias tag on the deployment too (via infra pipeline).
kevin: two quick checks: 1) does the provisioner call KMS with the same EncryptionContext keys (tenant_id / env / role) as used when the blob was encrypted? 2) Are we accidentally rekeying already-encrypted state vs creating a fresh key for new tokens?
maria: i checked the code path — the provisioner supplies {"tenant":"acme-inc","svc":"scim-provisioner"} as context. the encrypt calls from earlier versions had {"tenant":"acme-inc"} only. so there is a context key delta.
jen: that explains it — old blobs were encrypted with a smaller context; new unwraps expect the larger set, KMS rejects. Audit shows KMS ValidateContext failed.
david-oncall: immediate mitigation options?
kevin: two options: 1) revert the provisioner to the previous context usage (fast but risky if other services rely on new context) or 2) revert the alias pointer in KMS to the previous key for now (safer, faster rollback).
liz: i can revert alias pointer in KMS to the older CMK within 10m and monitor. doing it now.
maria: copying steps so i can follow: which alias to point to? we have alias/redwood/acme -> key-id-old vs key-id-new.
liz: alias currently points to key-id-new. i'm switching to key-id-old. will post when done.
jen: also we need an incident ticket and a retrospective — this is a change to encryption metadata that should've required a DB migration path.
liz: switched alias back to key-id-old at 18:10:07.
kevin: confirm by trying a local unwrap call against a sample blob?
maria: running small dry-run against the blocked user queue...
maria: provisioning resumed for the first 28 users, no 403s now. backlog draining.
david-oncall: nice. how many stuck items?
maria: ~412 users queued across three batches. i'll kick an on-demand backfill once we confirm no partial corruption.
jen: action items: 
- create incident ticket INC-2026-042 (sec + infra) for KMS context drift and rollout gaps
- add pre-rotation smoke test in infra CI that attempts to unwrap a few existing blobs for each tenant after alias swap
- improve release notes for KMS rotations to call out EncryptionContext schema changes
kevin: + add a canary step to the provisioner deployment that runs a small sample provision against a staging tenant before changing alias in prod.
liz: filing change rollback doc and will coordinate a safe re-rotation plan with maria and kevin.
maria: leaving this thread open until backfill completes and INC ticket is created. i'll post the incident link. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
kevin: follow-up — postmortem should include vuln/attack surface check: we altered context keys, ensure no elevation risk where an attacker could craft blobs to be accepted by new context.
jen: noted. tagging security review.
maria: incident created: INC-2026-042 (link internal) — backfill started at 18:18:00, monitoring logs for reoccurrence.
david-oncall: ping me if backlog > 1k or errors reappear. I'll keep oncall watch for next 2 hours.
maria: closing thread after backup validation. will file the postmortem draft tomorrow.
